tldr: The primary contribution is an exact finite-sample support frontier for causal treatment choice under calibrated target contamination. For arbitrary positive fixed arm sizes, the sharp upper odds permitting a deterministic treatment-one recommendation at the opposite unanimous cell are \(1\), \(\sqrt2\), \(\varphi\), and \(2\), in the four allocation classes of Theorem 2. Coordinated with these ceilings, the lower-frontier theorem proves \(\mathcal E_{2,M}=\mathcal E_{M,2}=[\ell_M,\varphi]\) for every integer \(M\ge7\). It computes \(\ell_M\) exactly by a finite semialgebraic program, supplies attaining count tables throughout the interval, and gives finite endpoint-state exclusion certificates below it. Exactness is algorithmic; a uniform closed formula is not asserted. Theorem 1 gives the separate closed-form \((3,3)\) interval, and Theorem 3 transports floor-attaining rules when contamination odds increase. The independent-assignment solution and qualitative design warning remain credited to \cite{Stoye2012LimitedValidity}. General balanced sufficiency and complete below-floor minimax values remain outside scope.
gap: \cite{Stoye2012LimitedValidity} solves the independent-assignment contamination decision problem.
